items.prompt:
When a moving object hits a still object, it transfers
A) color
B) energy
C) nothing
D) weight only

A moving marble hits a still marble. The still marble will
A) stay still
B) start to move
C) disappear
D) get colder

A crash makes a loud bang. Some energy of motion became
A) sound
B) a magnet
C) a color
D) nothing

steps: Some energy changed into sound energy.

items.prompt:
If you roll a marble faster into still marbles, they will move
A) less
B) more
C) the same
D) backward only

steps: A faster marble transfers more energy.

items.prompt:
After a moving marble hits a still one, the first marble
A) speeds up
B) slows down or stops
C) grows larger
D) changes color

steps: It gives away energy, so it slows.

items.prompt:
Besides sound, collisions can change energy of motion into
A) heat
B) water
C) light years
D) weight

A student predicts that in a crash the energy just disappears. The correct idea is that the energy
A) disappears
B) transfers to the other object and becomes sound and heat
C) turns into a new object
D) was never there
items.answer: B) transfers to the other object and becomes sound and heat

steps: Energy is transferred and changes form, not destroyed.

items.prompt:
Which is a good TESTABLE question about colliding marbles?
A) Are marbles pretty?
B) Will a faster marble push a still marble farther than a slow one?
C) Who owns the marbles?
D) What color should marbles be?
items.answer: B) Will a faster marble push a still marble farther than a slow one?

steps: A testable question compares measurable outcomes for different speeds.
